title: Arrays
description: Learn how to work with collections of data using arrays. Store multiple values, iterate through them, and manipulate array data.

sections.title: What are Arrays?
sections.content:
An **array** is a collection of elements of the same type, stored in contiguous memory.

- All elements must be the **same type**
- Elements are accessed by **index** (starting from 0)
- Arrays have a **fixed size** (determined at compile time)
- Very **efficient** for sequential access

sections.title: Array Syntax Comparison

languages.BPL:
local nums: int[5];           # Uninitialized
local arr: int[] = [1, 2, 3];  # Initialized
languages.JavaScript:
let nums = new Array(5);
let arr = [1, 2, 3];

sections.explanation: BPL uses type[size] for fixed arrays. The type comes first, followed by brackets with the size.

sections.title: Creating and Accessing Arrays
sections.expectedOutput:
First score: 85
Second score: 92
Last score: 88
Updated third score: 82

First price: $9.99
First flag: 1

lineExplanations.5: int[] with initializer - array size is determined from values (5 elements).
lineExplanations.13: Arrays are mutable - you can change individual elements.

sections.title: Iterating Through Arrays
sections.expectedOutput:
All numbers:
numbers[0] = 10
numbers[1] = 20
numbers[2] = 30
numbers[3] = 40
numbers[4] = 50

Sum: 150
Average: 30
Maximum: 50

lineExplanations.5: Keep track of array length - BPL doesn't have built-in .length.
lineExplanations.22: Start with first element as max, then compare rest.
lineExplanations.23: Start from index 1 since we already have index 0.

sections.title: Multi-Dimensional Arrays

lineExplanations.5: int[2][2] creates a 2D array (2 rows, 2 columns).
lineExplanations.6-7: Assign values to each element individually.
lineExplanations.14: Nested loops: outer for rows, inner for columns.
lineExplanations.15: matrix[i][j] - first index is row, second is column.

sections.title: Passing Arrays to Functions

lineExplanations.4: *int is a pointer to int - arrays decay to pointers.
lineExplanations.6: *(arr + i) accesses element at index i via pointer arithmetic.

sections.title: Array Bounds Warning!
sections.content:
⚠️ **BPL does NOT check array bounds by default!**

Accessing an index outside the array leads to **undefined behavior**:

```bpl
local arr: int[] = [1, 2, 3];  # Valid indices: 0, 1, 2

printf("%d", arr[5]);  # BAD! Index 5 doesn't exist
arr[10] = 42;          # BAD! Writing outside bounds
```

This can:
- Read garbage values
- Overwrite other variables
- Crash your program
- Create security vulnerabilities

**Always track your array sizes and validate indices!**

sections.title: Safe Array Access Pattern
sections.expectedOutput:
data[2]: 30
Warning: Index 10 out of bounds (0-4)
data[10]: -1
Updated data[1]: 25
Error: Cannot set index 100 (out of bounds)

lineExplanations.5: Check if index is negative or >= length.
lineExplanations.7: Return a default value for invalid indices.
lineExplanations.14: Return false if the set operation failed.

sections.title: Practice: Array Statistics
sections.instructions:
Write a program that:
1. Creates an array of 6 test scores: [78, 92, 85, 69, 95, 88]
2. Calculates and prints: minimum, maximum, sum, and average
3. Counts how many scores are >= 80 (passing)
sections.hint: Loop through the array, keeping track of min, max, and sum. Count passes with an if inside the loop.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ Arrays store multiple values of the **same type**

✅ Indices start at **0** (first element is arr[0])

✅ Use `type[]` with initializer or `type[size]` for fixed size

✅ **Track array length** - BPL doesn't have built-in .length

✅ **No bounds checking** - always validate indices!

✅ Arrays are passed as **pointers** to functions

✅ Use `int[][]` for 2D arrays (matrices)

questions.question: What is the index of the first element in an array?
questions.explanation: Arrays in BPL (and most languages) are 0-indexed. First element is at index 0.

questions.question: Given `local arr: int[] = [5, 10, 15, 20];`, what is arr[2]?
questions.explanation: arr[0]=5, arr[1]=10, arr[2]=15, arr[3]=20. Index 2 is the third element.

questions.question: What happens if you access arr[100] when arr has only 5 elements?
questions.explanation: BPL doesn't check bounds. Accessing invalid indices is undefined behavior.
